Functions of the Brain Stem

Midbrain, Pons & Medulla — muscle tone regulation, maintenance of equilibrium, and the vestibular system. Lecture by Dr. Hassan Salaheldeen.

🧠 CNS Neurology ⭐ High-Yield: UMN vs LMN tone 👂 Vestibular System 🩺 Clinical Correlations
1Brain Stem Overview

The brain stem is composed of three parts, from superior to inferior: the Midbrain, the Pons (literally "bridge"), and the Medulla oblongata. It sits between the cerebrum above and the spinal cord below.

Medulla oblongata: a direct continuation of the spinal cord (the spinal cord's other name is "spinal medulla"). As the spinal medulla enters the skull it undergoes elongation — hence the name "oblongata" (elongated medulla).
Sagittal section — the three brain stem components: Midbrain, Pons, and Medulla, continuous with the spinal cord below and the cerebellum posteriorly. This is a real brain photograph.
🔍 Click to enlarge
Overview diagram — relative position of the brain stem beneath the thalamus/hypothalamus and cerebellum, continuous with the spinal cord.

2The 5 Core Functions of the Brain Stem
  1. Maintenance of muscle tone — via control of the stretch reflex. The stretch reflex is a spinal reflex, but it is subject to facilitatory and inhibitory impulses from the brain, including the brain stem.
  2. Maintenance of equilibrium — via the Vestibular nucleus and the Reticular formation. Note the pattern: Vestibular apparatus, Vestibular nucleus, Vestibulocerebellum — all three relate to equilibrium.
  3. Contains the vital centers for regulation of Respiration, the Cardiovascular system (Vasomotor, Cardioinhibitory, Cardioacceleratory areas), and GIT centers (Salivary nucleus, Swallowing center) — all located in the Medulla.
  4. Connects sensory and motor brain areas with the spinal cord — e.g. the Corticospinal and Corticobulbar tracts descend through the brain stem; about 80% of corticospinal fibers decussate in the Medulla. The brain stem also contains the motor nuclei of the cranial nerves.
  5. Contains the Reticular Activating System (RAS) — a network of neurons with a net-like ("reticular") structure containing sensory, motor, and interneurons. It is activated by diverse stimuli (touch, pain, thermal, etc.) and sends non-specific impulses to the cortex to maintain general cortical excitability. This links the RAS to the sleep–wakefulness cycle, in addition to its relationship with the hypothalamus.
🧠 Quick recall
Think "M-E-V-C-R": Muscle tone · Equilibrium · Vital centers (resp/CVS/GIT) · Connects sensory-motor pathways · Reticular Activating System.
3Muscle Tone — Definition & Clinical Testing
Muscle tone = state of sustained, partial contraction of skeletal muscle that offers resistance to stretch.

No muscle in the living body is ever in a state of complete relaxation — every muscle maintains a partial, ongoing contraction. This is why a completely relaxed body (e.g., a sleeping person being carried, or a body after rigor mortis has passed) feels noticeably heavier to lift: tone normally helps support and distribute body weight, and its complete absence removes that support.

🩺 How to clinically examine tone

The examiner passively moves a patient's joint and assesses the resistance to stretch:

Resistance foundInterpretation
Higher than normalHypertonia
AbsentAtonia
Lower than normalHypotonia
NormalNormal tone
4Gamma Motor Neuron & the Muscle Spindle

Muscle tone increases with increased Gamma (γ) motor neuron discharge, and decreases with decreased discharge — this is the final common pathway controlling tone.

The Gamma motor neuron is also called the "small motor neuron." In sensory/motor classification it is purely motor (not sensory). It innervates the terminal (polar) contractile parts of the muscle spindle's intrafusal fibers.

Muscle spindle anatomy: the central portion is non-contractile and houses the receptor (intrafusal fibers — Nuclear Bag or Nuclear Chain type). The terminal (polar) portions are contractile and attach to the tendon; these are innervated by the Gamma motor neuron. Although the spindle is a receptor, it also receives an efferent (motor) input — and this efferent input is what controls tone.
Dynamic vs. static response of the stretch reflex
Tap the tendon
→
Contraction (e.g. biceps flexion / triceps extension)
→
"Dynamic response" — tests reflex presence
Brain stem–driven γ discharge
→
Continuous background activity
→
"Static response" — maintains muscle tone

The reflex elicited by tapping a tendon (dynamic response) tests whether the reflex arc is intact, but it is the continuous static response, driven by Gamma motor neuron discharge linked to the brain stem, that actually maintains resting muscle tone.

5Facilitatory Centers for Muscle Tone

The brain stem contains regulatory areas for the Gamma motor neuron and hence for muscle tone. There are two facilitatory areas and one inhibitory area.

A) Facilitatory Pontine Reticular Formation
  • Increases Gamma motor neuron discharge and tone.
  • Has intrinsic (spontaneous) activity — it works even if isolated from higher centers (e.g., after decerebration, it remains active).
  • Also activated by impulses from:
    • Primary motor area (Area 4) of the cerebral cortex
    • Vestibular nucleus (in the brain stem itself)
    • Deep cerebellar nuclei
⭐ High-Yield link
These three sources — Area 4, Vestibular nucleus, and Deep cerebellar nuclei — are, together with the Pontine reticular formation itself, the four facilitatory contributors to tone. A massive/diffuse cerebellar lesion that involves the deep cerebellar nuclei removes their facilitatory drive → Hypotonia.
Facilitatory supraspinal centers — Area 4 (pyramidal tract), Pontine reticular formation, Cerebellar cortex, and Vestibular nucleus all provide (+) facilitatory input converging on the Gamma motor neuron.
🔍 Click to enlarge
6Inhibitory Medullary Reticular Formation
  • Decreases Gamma motor neuron discharge and muscle tone.
  • Has NO intrinsic activity — unlike the pontine facilitatory center, it strictly depends on incoming impulses to function.
  • Depends on impulses from:
    • Area 4S — a small suppressor strip just in front of Area 4; a physiological (not strictly anatomical) area with a small number of neurons but a strong suppressor effect
    • Basal ganglia
    • Some areas of the cerebellar cortex
🩺 Why Upper Motor Neuron lesions cause Hypertonia
Area 4S fibers descend through the Internal capsule. A lesion of the internal capsule (classic UMN lesion) interrupts these fibers, so the Medullary (inhibitory) reticular formation loses its activating input and becomes functionally silent — even though the inhibitory center itself is structurally intact. Meanwhile, the Pontine facilitatory center is unaffected (or even unopposed) because it has intrinsic activity and does not depend on cortical input via the internal capsule. The result: facilitatory drive dominates → Hypertonia. If the lesion is instead localized to the cortex itself (rather than internal capsule), the effect may still produce Hypertonia via loss of Area 4S output; if in Basal ganglia or specific cerebellar cortical areas, it likewise removes inhibitory drive.
Inhibitory supraspinal centers — Inhibitory cortical motor areas (Area 4S), Basal ganglia, and Red nucleus converge on the Medullary reticular formation, which sends (−) inhibitory input to the Gamma motor neuron.
🔍 Click to enlarge
7The Facilitatory–Inhibitory Balance

Normal muscle tone — which maintains our posture — depends on a balance between facilitatory and inhibitory effects on the Gamma motor neuron.

Balance shiftResult
Facilitatory > InhibitoryHypertonia
Inhibitory > FacilitatoryHypotonia
⭐ Putting it together — Upper Motor Neuron lesion
Consistently presents with Hypertonia. This relates to loss of cortical inhibitory input (specifically from Area 4S) to the Medullary reticular formation, which removes inhibition and allows facilitatory centers (with their intrinsic activity) to dominate unopposed.

(Note from lecture: Lower motor neuron lesions and Upper motor neuron lesions during neural shock both classically produce Hypotonia; after neural shock resolves, the UMN lesion pattern converts to Hypertonia as described above. Basal ganglia and cerebellar tone disorders are covered in their dedicated lectures.)

8Functions of Muscle Tone
  1. Maintenance of body posture — Standing upright ("orthostatic posture") depends on the extensor tone of the axial muscles dominating over flexor tone. ("Ortho-" = straight/upright, as in "orthopedic" = bone-straightening.)
  2. Participates in the genesis and regulation of body temperature — Loss of tone (along with cessation of metabolism) contributes to body cooling after death.
  3. Increases venous return to the heart — particularly relevant to the parts of the body below the level of the heart (lower limbs, abdomen); muscle contraction/tone helps pump venous blood upward.
  4. Tone of abdominal muscles holds the viscera in place — keeping the abdominal wall flat rather than protuberant/pendulous. Clinical correlation: in Cushing syndrome, increased fat deposition stretches the abdominal wall, producing a "pendulous abdomen."
9Maintenance of Equilibrium — the Vestibular Apparatus

The receptors for equilibrium are found in the vestibular apparatus, located within the membranous labyrinth of the inner ear.

The inner ear's scientific name is the Labyrinth, composed of two parts: an outer Bony labyrinth and an inner Membranous labyrinth. They are separated from each other by Perilymph. Inside the membranous labyrinth is Endolymph — a potassium-rich fluid.
The ear — outer, middle, and inner ear. The Cochlea (hearing) is a separate structure from the vestibular apparatus (equilibrium), though both share cranial nerve VIII (Vestibulocochlear nerve) and the inner ear space.
🔍 Click to enlarge
Membranous labyrinth — Semicircular canals with Crista ampullaris in each ampulla (rotation receptors); Utricle and Saccule with Maculae and statoconia (static/linear motion receptors).
🔍 Click to enlarge
10Two Receptor Types of the Vestibular Apparatus
1️⃣ Maculae / Otolithic organs

Located in the Utricle and Saccule. Responsible for:

  • Static equilibrium — e.g., maintaining balance while sitting or standing, resisting gravity's pull.
  • Linear motion equilibrium — e.g., the sensation when a car brakes suddenly: without this system, your body would continue forward at its prior momentum unopposed.
2️⃣ Crista ampullaris

Located in the ampulla (a dilated region) of each Semicircular canal — hence the name "ampullaris."

  • Responsible for equilibrium during rotation (angular motion) — e.g., the dizziness felt getting off a spinning playground ride.
The role of Endolymph movement

Endolymph moves under the force of gravity during static positioning, and under momentum/inertia during linear or rotational motion — it is this movement of endolymph that mechanically stimulates the receptor hair cells. Because endolymph lags behind the body's own acceleration or deceleration, disturbance in balance sensation classically occurs at the start and end of motion — once endolymph "catches up" to a constant velocity, no further disturbance is sensed.

11Hair Cell Stimulation Mechanism

Each receptor region contains Hair cells, named for their cilia. Each hair cell has a bundle of cilia: one long Kinocilium (K) and a group of shorter Stereocilia (S).

Endolymph movement
→
Kinocilium bends against Stereocilia
→
Ion channels open
→
Receptor potential
→
Summation → Action potential

The resulting action potential travels via the vestibular branch of the Vestibulocochlear nerve (Cranial nerve VIII). (Recall: the Cochlear branch of CN VIII carries hearing information from the cochlea; the Vestibular branch carries equilibrium information from the vestibular apparatus.)

Inner ear schematic — enlarged views of the Cupula (crista ampullaris receptor in the semicircular canal) and the Otolithic membrane (macula receptor of the saccule/utricle), alongside the cochlea for comparison.
🔍 Click to enlarge
Hair cell structure — the Kinocilium (K) and Stereocilia (S) bundle; bending this bundle toward the kinocilium opens mechanically-gated ion channels, generating a receptor potential.

12Vestibular Pathway

Fibers of the vestibular nerve terminate in the ipsilateral Vestibular nucleus (same side).

A) From the Semicircular canals (rotation)
Semicircular canals
→
Brain stem vestibular region
→
CN III (Oculomotor), IV (Trochlear), VI (Abducens)
→
Reflex eye movements during rotation

These reflex eye movements are normal during active rotation (eyes track to maintain the prior visual scene). If similar rhythmic eye movement (Nystagmus) is seen without any rotation occurring, this indicates mal-equilibrium.

B) From the Utricle & Saccule (linear motion & static equilibrium)
Utricle & Saccule
→
Cerebellum (via Vestibulocerebellar tract → Flocculonodular lobe / "Vestibulocerebellum")
Utricle & Saccule
→
Spinal cord (via Vestibulospinal tract)
Utricle & Saccule
→
Reticular formation
→
Spinal cord (via Reticulospinal tract)
C) To conscious sensation

Vestibular nuclei also project to the Thalamus, which relays to the primary somatosensory cortex, giving conscious spatial/positional sensation.

Vestibular pathway (right half of diagram) — vestibular ganglion → ipsilateral vestibular nuclei → cranial nerves III/IV/VI, cerebellum, vestibulospinal tracts, and thalamus → somatosensory cortex.
🔍 Click to enlarge
🥅 Worked example — kicking a football / avoiding a puddle

To kick with the right leg, you must stand and balance on the left leg. In this instant, the Reticular formation and Vestibular nucleus increase facilitatory impulses to the left extensors (supporting/standing leg) and decrease impulses to the right extensors (kicking leg, which needs to flex/lift). The same logic applies when you suddenly lift one foot to avoid a puddle or hole — tone shifts instantly to the supporting leg via the Vestibulospinal and Reticulospinal tracts.

13Anti-Gravity Muscles & Equilibrium Maintenance

Equilibrium is maintained by changes in the tone of anti-gravity muscles, mediated by impulses from the Vestibulospinal and Reticulospinal tracts.

Body regionAnti-gravity muscle group
Back & Lower limbExtensors (the main anti-gravity muscles for equilibrium)
Upper limbFlexors
Clinical illustration: a person falling asleep while holding a cup or phone will drop it as tone is lost — because the upper-limb anti-gravity (flexor) tone that was holding the object flexed disappears with relaxation.
The brain stem maintains equilibrium during:
  • Station (static standing/sitting posture)
  • Linear motion (e.g., a car braking — the body's momentum is checked and corrected)
  • Rotation (e.g., on a boat/sea motion, or spinning)
14Mal-Equilibrium
Causes
  • Heavy/irregular traffic motion — the common cause of Motion sickness (car, ship, plane). Rough braking and turning (non-smooth motion) provoke it; smooth motion is much less likely to.
  • Caloric stimulation — used diagnostically (see below).
🩺 Motion sickness prevention tip
Avoid sitting in the back seat, and avoid repeatedly shifting gaze between the moving exterior scenery and the stationary interior of the vehicle. Alternating between "outside looks like it's moving, but is actually still" and "inside looks still, but is moving with you" produces a sensory mismatch between visual and vestibular input, which is what generates mal-equilibrium and nausea.
Autonomic responses (Motion sickness)

Because the brain stem also houses the swallowing, salivation, respiratory, and cardiovascular centers, motion sickness can trigger tachycardia, blood pressure changes, nausea, vomiting, and sweating — all autonomic responses linked to brain stem centers.

Caloric stimulation testing

Cold liquid instilled into the ear canal is used clinically to test brain stem viability in comatose or suspected brain-dead patients. If the brain stem is intact, reflex eye movement (Nystagmus) occurs; absence of this reflex suggests brain stem non-function.

Vertigo

A false sensation of rotation — either the patient feels they themselves are spinning, or that their surroundings are spinning — in the absence of actual rotation. Normally felt briefly at the start and end of rotation, because endolymph continues moving by momentum for a short time after the body itself has stopped (or before it has caught up at the start).

Nystagmus

Rapid, to-and-fro eye movement. Normally observed at the start and end of rotation (reflexive eye tracking). If observed without any actual rotation, it is a feature of mal-equilibrium.

All forms of mal-equilibrium can ultimately lead to falling, under the force of gravity, if balance is not restored.

15High-Yield Exam Pearls
⭐⭐⭐ Must Know
Upper motor neuron (UMN) lesions consistently present with Hypertonia. This is highly testable and relates to loss of cortical inhibitory input (specifically from Area 4S) to the Medullary reticular formation, allowing the facilitatory centers to dominate.
⭐⭐ High Yield
Facilitatory pontine reticular formation: Has intrinsic (spontaneous) activity and consistently increases Gamma motor neuron discharge. It works independently even if isolated from higher centers.
⭐⭐ High Yield
Inhibitory medullary reticular formation: Has NO intrinsic activity. It strictly relies on activation from higher centers (like Area 4S and Basal ganglia) to decrease Gamma motor neuron discharge.
⭐⭐ High Yield
Deep cerebellar nuclei lesions: Massive or diffuse cerebellar lesions involving the deep nuclei characteristically present with Hypotonia.
⭐⭐⭐ Must Know — Receptors of Equilibrium
  • Maculae / Otolithic organs (Utricle and Saccule): static equilibrium (gravity/posture) and linear motion (e.g., stopping suddenly in a car).
  • Crista ampullaris (in Semicircular canals): equilibrium during angular motion / rotation.
⭐⭐ High Yield
Vestibular pathway to eye muscles: Fibers from the semicircular canals project via the brain stem to cranial nerves III (Oculomotor), IV (Trochlear), and VI (Abducens) to control rapid eye movements (Nystagmus) during rotation.
⭐ Very Important
Anti-gravity muscles: The primary anti-gravity muscles maintaining upright (orthostatic) posture are the extensors of the back and lower limbs, and the flexors of the upper limbs.
16Clinical Pearls
🩺 Examining muscle tone
Tone is the resistance of muscle to stretch. To clinically assess tone, passively move a patient's joint. High resistance = Hypertonia; low resistance = Hypotonia; no resistance = Atonia.
🩺 Weight of an atonic patient
A completely relaxed or deceased person (post rigor-mortis) feels significantly heavier to lift, because the natural, sustained partial contraction (tone) that normally assists in distributing body weight and maintaining posture is completely absent.
🩺 Motion sickness prevention
To minimize motion sickness while traveling in a vehicle, avoid sitting in the back or constantly shifting your gaze between stationary interior objects and moving exterior scenery, as this causes a sensory mismatch in the vestibular system.
🩺 Caloric stimulation testing
Instilling cold liquid into the ear canal (Caloric stimulation) can be used clinically to check for brain stem viability in comatose or suspected brain-dead patients. An intact brain stem will produce reflex eye movements (Nystagmus).
🩺 Clinical presentation of vertigo
Vertigo is strictly defined as a false sensation of rotation (either the patient feels they are spinning, or the room is spinning) when no actual movement is occurring. It is normal briefly after stopping a rapid rotation due to continued movement of the endolymph fluid.

اي سيشن تقريبا 50 دقيقة. الاولى حتكون عن ال Brain stem، والثانية حتكون عن ال Basal ganglia، والأخيرة بعد الظهر حتكون عن ال Cerebellum.

ال Brain stem طبعا ال Midbrain وال Pons وال Medulla. حنأخذ اول جزء المرة التانية دي حتكون ال CNS والثانية حتكون عن ال Basal ganglia وبعدين حنأخذ حتة من ال Cerebellum. ده ال component حق ال Brain stem في ال general كده وال level بتاعته. دي المنطقة حقتنا اللي حنتكلم فيها.

دي ال first step، بتبدأ من ال Medulla oblongata. وال Medulla oblongata طبعا هي مواصلة لل Spinal cord. ال Spinal cord اسمه التاني ال Spinal medulla، النخاع الشوكي. لما نخش ال Skull بيحصل ليه elongation، قاموا سموه Medulla oblongata. يعني هو نخاع، كان نخاع شوكي وبقى نخاع مستطيل. ده ليه؟ لانه حصل ليه elongation. بتبدأ ال Medulla oblongata وده جزء منه، من ال Brain بعد ال Pons اللي هو زي الجسر، حتى ال Midbrain فوق.

ده ال Sagittal section بورينا الوضع بتاع ال Brain stem. تلاتة مكونات، ال Medulla، هنا ال Pons هنا وال Midbrain فوق. دي الموقعية بتاعتنا.

ال function بتاعت ال Brain stem فيها وظائف: واحدة منها maintenance of the muscle tone، حفظ ال Muscle tone، زي اللي هو عبر الكنترول بتاعه لل Stretch reflex. طبعا ال Stretch reflex هي Spinal reflex لكنها subjected ب facilitatory و inhibitory impulse من ال Brain including the Brain stem. عشان كده بتلعب دور رئيسي جدا في موضوع ال Muscle tone والكنترول بتاع ال Stretch reflex.

الحاجة التانية maintenance of equilibrium، حفظ التوازن. عندنا منطقة اسمها ال Vestibular nucleus، ده غير موضوع ال Reticular formation ودوره في ال Equilibrium. فاي حاجة فيها vestibulo طبعا Equilibrium: Vestibular apparatus، Vestibular nucleus، Vestibulocerebellum. تلاتة اشياء بادية ب vestibulo كلها شغالة بال Equilibrium.

الحاجة التالتة contain the vital centers، سنتر لل regulation بتاع ال Respiration في ال Medulla. Cardiovascular center اللي هي ال circulation سواء كان Vasomotor area، Cardioinhibitory area، Cardioacceleratory area كلها في ال Medulla. ال سنتر بتاعت ال GIT، ال Salivary nucleus، ال Swallowing، كده كلها فيه.

تاني الوظيفة connect the sensory وال motor brain areas with the spinal cord. ال Corticospinal tract، Corticobulbar tract Motor نزلت في ال Brain stem وفي ال Medulla 80% منها حصل تقاطع. فال Brain stem عندنا ال Motor nuclei بتاعت ال Cranial nerves في ال Midbrain سواء كان في ال Pons ولا ال Medulla، دي كلها connection مع ال Spinal cord و connection مع ال Cranial nerves.

contain Reticular Activating System يسموه RAS. عبارة عن network of neurons ماخدة Reticular structure شكلها شبكة، عشان كده بيسموه بالعربي التكوين الشبكي. فيها Sensory neuron و Motor neuron و Interneuron. وهذا ال RAS affected بال stimuli المختلفة سواء كان touch، pain، thermal، او غيره. ودي بتمشي تودي impulses non-specific لل Cortex عشان تحفظ ال general excitability بتاعت ال Cortex. عشان كده هذا ال system عنده علاقة بالموضوع بتاع ال Sleep او Wakefulness cycle، الدورة بتاعت النوم والاستيقاظ، بيسموها Dark-light cycle او Sleep-wakefulness cycle عندها علاقة مع ال Reticular formation، غير علاقتها مع ال Hypothalamus.

نبدأ بال Muscle tone. ال definition بتاعه: state of sustained partial contraction لل Skeletal muscle that offer the resistance to stretch. عشان كده لما نقول ال Stretch reflex بتحفظ ال Muscle tone لانه ال Stretch حينبه ال Muscle spindle. ال Muscle spindle هتقوم تعمل potential، تمشي عن طريق ال Afferent، تخش ال Spinal cord، طبعا هي monosynaptic ترتبط مع ال Efferent، تمشي للعضلة تعمل Contraction.

عشان كده العضلات مهما يكون ما عندها Complete relaxation. ما عندك اي عضلة في جسمك في حالة Complete relaxation، اي عضلة في حالة Contraction لكنه partial. لكن بعد ما تنتهي الحياة، نجي لل Relaxation (بعد Rigor mortis). التون بيخفف الوزن، الـContraction بيخلي وزنك خفيف، لكن لما التون يكون مافي خلاص، الجنازة تقيلة، لانه مافي tone خلاص.

طيب نحن قلنا ال tone هو resistance of muscle لل stretch. فانت داير تختبر ال tone، تشوف ال resistance: عالية Hypertonia، مافي Atonia، ضعيفة Hypotonia، عادية Normal tone.

تختبر ال tone بانك تتحرك ال joint، تشوفها، لو فيها مقاومة اكتر من اللازم تقول Hypertonia. ال tone increase by increasing Gamma motor neuron discharge، والعكس صحيح.

شنو هو ال Gamma motor neuron؟ برضه بيسموه small motor neuron، motor فقط (مش sensory). وده اللي بيعمل innervation لل terminal part بتاعت ال Muscle spindle. ال Muscle spindle عندها central portion، ده site of the receptor، فيه ال Intrafusal fiber (Nuclear bag او Nuclear chain). ال terminal بتاعها الموصل مع ال tendon، وده contractile. اما ال central، non-contractile بتاع ال receptor. الجزء ال contractile ده بيـ innervated بال Gamma motor neuron. فمع انها receptor، لكنها بتستقبل efferent، وده مهم لموضوع ال tone.

يعني لما تعمل ال Stretch reflex examination وتضرب ال tendon، بتحصل contraction (dynamic response)، لكن ال Stretch reflex اللي بتحفظ ال Muscle tone علاقتها بال Gamma motor neuron discharge المربوط بال Brain stem. كل ما ال Gamma motor neuron discharge زاد، زاد ال tone، وكل ما نقص نقص ال tone.

في ال Stretch reflex عندك two response: dynamic response و static response. ال static response دي الشغالة طوالي، دي بتاعت ال tone ودي المربوطة بال Gamma motor neuron المربوط بال Brain stem. اما ال dynamic response دي داير تشوف في reflex موجودة ولا لا.

ال Brain stem عنده regulatory area لهذا ال Gamma motor neuron وبالتالي لل Muscle tone: facilitatory area (Facilitatory pontine reticular formation) و Vestibular nucleus، وInhibitory medullary reticular formation.

ال Facilitatory pontine reticular formation: increase ال Gamma motor neuron discharge والا ما كان يكون facilitatory. has intrinsic activity، عنده نشاط ذاتي، داخلي المنشأ، حتى لو عملت decerebration بيكون شغال. عشان كده في حالة ال Upper motor neuron lesion كان شغال. عنده spontaneous activity. also activated by impulses from: Primary motor area (Area 4) بتاعت ال Cerebral cortex، Vestibular nucleus في ال Brain stem نفسه، وال Deep cerebellar nuclei. التلاتة ديل facilitatory لل Muscle tone ولل Gamma motor neuron. لو كان ال Cerebellum حصل فيها massive lesion involving ال Deep nuclei، بيؤدي لـ Hypotonia. عشان كده lesion بتاع ال Cerebellum ال massive وال diffuse characterized بـ Hypotonia.

ال Inhibitory medullary reticular formation: بينقص ال Gamma motor neuron discharge والا ما كان يكون inhibitory. has no intrinsic activity، يعتمد على ال impulses. عشان يعمل inhibition لل Gamma motor neuron وينقص ال tone، داير حاجة تعمله activation من ال Area 4S: Small suppressor strip just in front of Area 4، وظيفته فسيولوجيك rather than anatomic. neuron بسيطة جدا لكن عندها strong effect (suppressor). اذا هي بتنشط ال Reticular formation عشان يعمل inhibition لل Gamma motor neuron.

وده الخلانا نقول لما يكون عندنا Upper motor neuron lesion حيكون عندنا Hypertonia. لانه فقدنا ده. فقدنا ده، وده اقوى من ال facilitatory. لما يكون في lesion فقدناهم، لانها معتمدة على fibers الجاياها من Area 4S حتمر بال Internal capsule وحتكون ال lesion شملها. بقت ال Medullary reticular formation الدائرة تعمل inhibition لل Muscle tone، هي ذاتها ما شغالة، لانها ما بتشتغل الا بال fibers البتجيها عبر ال Internal capsule، لكن بتاع ال Pons ما تأثر لانه لو جاته ال fibers خير وبركة، ولو ما جاته هو شغال براه. من ال Basal ganglia، ومن بعض ال areas في ال Cerebellar cortex. لو ال lesion كان localized في الكورتكس ممكن التأثير يكون Hypertonia.

Normal muscle tone حافظين ال posture بتاعنا due لل balance between the effect بتاعت ال facilitatory وال inhibitory. لو واحدة اتغلبت على التانية، يحصل المشكلة بتاعت التون. لو ال facilitatory غلبت ال inhibitory، Hypertonia. ولو العكس، Hypotonia.

الفنكشن بتاعت ال Muscle tone: اول حاجة excellent ال posture، القوام. نحن عندنا upright posture سواء واقفين او قاعدين. لما تكون واقف، التون بتاع ال extensor بتاعت ال axial متغلب على ال flexor، عشان كده عندك upright posture، اسمه orthostatic posture. ortho دايما معناها عديل، قايم، orthostatic. جات منها orthopedic. ده بيحفظها ليك ال extensor اللي هي ال axial muscle.

تاني participate في ال genesis وال regulation of body temperature. يقول لك الزول ده مات جسمه برد، لانه بعد كده ما عنده contraction لا partial ولا full. واحد من الحاجات اللي وقفت الحرارة انه بقى مافي tone، غير انه وقف ال metabolism.

increase ال venous return لل heart، خاصة للاجزاء اللي تحت القلب، لانه ال venous return جاي من ال lower limb وال abdomen، والتون بتاع ال contraction بيرفع الدم لفوق.

ال Tone بتاع ال Abdominal muscle بيـ hold ال viscera in place، بيحفظ لك ال viscera في محلها، بيخلي البطن تبقى مستقيمة، ما تكون pendulous. عشان كده في Cushing syndrome بنقول عنده pendulous abdomen، لانه زادت الدهون فهتشد شوية وتخلي البطون تطلع من حتتها.

ال cause بتاعت ال Hypotonia وال Hypertonia: ال Lower motor neuron lesion بيعمل Hypotonia. وال Upper motor neuron lesion بيعمل Hypotonia during the Neural shock. اما بعد ال Neural shock ال upper بيعمل Hypertonia.

maintenance of equilibrium، حفظ التوازن. ال receptor بتاعت ال Equilibrium found في ال Vestibular apparatus، موجود في ال inner ear. ال inner ear اسمها العلمي ال Labyrinth، مكونة من جزئين: Bony labyrinth، وداخل ليه Membranous labyrinth. الاثنين مفصولات بـ Perilymph. وجوه ال Membranous labyrinth عندنا Endolymph.

بتشمل receptor: ال Maculae وال Otolithic organ، دي receptor لل static equilibrium وال linear motion equilibrium. static equilibrium يعني قعدتك ووقفتك وحفظ التوازن.

اما linear motion: لما السواق يعمل فرامل فجأة، كنت ماشي بسرعة 80 رجعها 30، لكن جسمك بمشي بال 80 لحظة، لولا هذا ال system كنت طرت بالاقزاز. الرجعة دي هي شغل هذا ال receptor.

Crista ampullaris موجودة في ال Semicircular canals، في منطقة dilated اسمها ampulla، عشان كده سموها Crista ampullaris. مسؤولة عن equilibrium during rotation. زي الطفل في الملاهي لما ينزل من الالعاب الدوارة، شايف روحه مدور. لولا هذا ال system طوالي هيقع.

ال Membranous labyrinth is filled with potassium-rich Endolymph. حركة ال endolymph هي اللي بتحرك ال receptor. move by force of gravity اثناء ال station، وبالموشن اثناء rotation او linear. عشان كده في البداية وفي النهاية بيحصل خلل في التوازن، لكن مجرد ما ال endolymph يبقى ماشي مع سرعتك، ما بيكون في اي خلل. عشان كده الطفل لما ينزل من الدوران بيحصل عنده vertigo ودوار في اللحظات دي، لانه بيحصل مع بداية ونهاية ال rotation.

ال Cochlea بتاعت ال hearing. ال Semicircular canals التلاتة موجودين في تلاتة اتجاهات (كل واحد بيتعامد على التاني). عندنا ال Utricle وال Saccule فيهم ال receptors بتاعت ال linear motion وال static (ال Maculae / Otolithic organ).

ال Hair cell الموجودة في ال receptor عندها cilia: K اختصار Kinocilium، وS اختصار Stereocilia. لما ال Kinocilium يمشي على ال Stereocilia بيحصل stimulation لل receptor، تفتح channels، يحصل generation لل Receptor potential، وال summation بتديك Action potential. دي حتخش في ال vestibular branch of the Vestibulocochlear nerve (CN 8)، اللي بيخدم ال hearing وال equilibrium. Cochlear branch من ال cochlea (hearing)، Vestibular branch من ال vestibular apparatus (equilibrium).

ال Vestibular pathway: fibers بتاعت ال vestibular nerve terminate في ال ipsilateral Vestibular nucleus. معظم fibers ال Semicircular canals (rotation) بتمشي لمنطقة في ال Brain stem بعدين project لل Cranial nerve 3 (Oculomotor)، 4 (Trochlear)، 6 (Abducens)، مسؤولين عن eye movement اثناء ال rotation. لو حصل mal-equilibrium بتلقى العين بتتحرك (Nystagmus) بدون rotation فعلية، دي مشكلة. لكن لو في rotation فعلية، حركة العين دي طبيعية.

معظم fibers ال Utricle وال Saccule project لل Cerebellum عن طريق Vestibulocerebellar tract لمنطقة اسمها Vestibulocerebellum (Flocculonodular lobe). وبرضو تمشي لل spinal cord عن طريق Vestibulospinal tract، ولل reticular formation ومنه لل spinal cord عن طريق Reticulospinal tract.

ال Vestibular nuclei also project لل Thalamus، ومن ال Thalamus لل primary somatosensory cortex.

مثال: لاعب كورة داير يهدف برجله اليمين، لازم يقيف على رجله الشمال. ال Reticular formation وال Vestibular nucleus بتزيد ال facilitatory impulse لل extensor بتاعت الشمال وتنقص بتاع اليمين. نفس القصة لو لقيت طين قدامك وحتقيف على الرجل التانية.

ال equilibrium بيتحفظ بتغيير في ال tone of anti-gravity muscles عن طريق ال Vestibulospinal وال Reticulospinal. ال main anti-gravity muscle فور equilibrium هم extensor of the back وال lower limb. اما anti-gravity muscle بتاعت upper limb هي flexor. عشان كده الواحد لو نايم ماسك حاجة، التون اتفقد، بتقع منه.

ال Brain stem maintain equilibrium during: station، linear motion، وrotation.

ال mal-equilibrium can result from: heavy traffic (Motion sickness) — سيارة، سفينة، طيارة. الفرامل القوية والحركة القوية بتعمل هجة. اذا داير تتفادى Motion sickness ما تركب ورا، لانك بتعاين بره (شجر واقف بس شايفه متحرك) وجوه (منظر ثابت لكنه متحرك بالنسبة لك)، بيحصل mismatching لل receptor.

ال mal-equilibrium بتاع ال Motion sickness فيه autonomic responses: tachycardia، change في ال blood pressure، vomiting، nausea، sweating، لانها مربوطة بال Brain stem (centers بتاعت swallowing، salivation، respiration، cardiovascular).

ال Caloric stimulation: يقطرون حاجة باردة في الاذن، لو العيون اتحركت (Nystagmus) الزول حي، لو ما اتحركت خلاص. بيستعملوه كتيست لفحص حيوية ال Brain stem.

المظاهر بتاعت ال mal-equilibrium: Vertigo: false sensation of rotation in absence of actual rotation. بيحصل normally during the start and end of rotation. Nystagmus: rapid eye movement to and fro، normally observed at start and end of rotation. ال mal-equilibrium كلها بتؤدي لـ falling down by force of gravity.
